title: Raising the bar: evidence-first debates (sources, standards, and shared ground)

The real danger here isn't just misinformation — it's that vulnerable people with treatable cancers might delay or refuse evidence-based treatment. title: PSA: No, pineapple juice does NOT cure blood cancer. Stop sharing that garbage before someone skips chemo.
content:

My aunt has CLL (chronic lymphocytic leukemia) and someone in her church group literally told her to stop treatment and drink pineapple juice instead. I am so tired of this.

Let me break this down:

1) The claim usually references bromelain, an enzyme in pineapple. Yes, there are a handful of in-vitro studies (meaning in a petri dish, not in a human body) where bromelain showed some anti-tumor properties. But guess what? Bleach kills cancer cells in a petri dish too. That doesn't make it medicine.

2) There is literally ZERO clinical trial evidence that pineapple juice treats any form of cancer in living humans. None. The National Cancer Institute does not list it as a treatment. No oncologist on earth is prescribing Dole cans.

3) AFP Fact Check investigated this specific claim and spoke with actual oncologists and cancer researchers. Dr. Ian Olver, a former CEO of the Cancer Council Australia, called the claim 'completely unfounded.' Multiple hematologists confirmed there is no mechanism by which drinking pineapple juice could eliminate malignant blood cells.

4) The viral posts often claim pineapple is '10,000 times stronger than chemo.' This number is completely fabricated. It doesn't come from any study, anywhere, ever.

The real danger here isn't just misinformation — it's that vulnerable people with treatable cancers might delay or refuse evidence-based treatment. Blood cancers like leukemia and lymphoma have seen massive improvements in survival rates thanks to modern medicine. Telling someone to swap that for fruit juice is genuinely dangerous.

If you see someone sharing this, please push back. Lives could literally depend on it.

Before you scroll past this, just hear me out. I spent the last three months going down this rabbit hole after my cousin was diagnosed with early-stage leukemia and I started looking into everything.

Pineapple contains an enzyme called bromelain. It's been studied since the 1970s. There are peer-reviewed papers showing that bromelain has direct cytotoxic effects on cancer cells — meaning it literally breaks them apart. One study from the journal Planta Medica found that bromelain outperformed 5-fluorouracil (a common chemo drug) in an animal tumor model. Let that sink in. A natural fruit enzyme outperformed chemotherapy.

So why isn't this front-page news? Follow the money. The global oncology drug market is worth over $200 BILLION per year. You think Pfizer and Roche want you to know that something you can buy for $3 at the grocery store might fight cancer? They'd lose everything.

I'm not saying throw away your doctor's advice overnight. But I AM saying the medical establishment has a financial incentive to suppress natural alternatives. There are clinics in Mexico and Germany that use bromelain-based protocols alongside other natural treatments, and the recovery stories coming out of those places are incredible.

My cousin started drinking fresh pineapple juice daily — not the processed stuff, FRESH — along with turmeric and ginger. His next blood panel showed improvement. Coincidence? Maybe. But maybe not.

The indigenous peoples of South America have used pineapple medicinally for centuries. We act like modern Western medicine invented healing, but nature had the answers long before Big Pharma started patenting molecules.

Do your own research. Look into bromelain studies yourself. The information is out there if you're willing to look past what the mainstream wants you to believe. They can't patent a pineapple, and that's exactly why they'll never tell you the truth.

title: Our government spends £29,900/year on illegal immigrants while our pensioners who built this country scrape by on £6,000. Let that sink in.
content:
Just came across these figures and honestly I feel physically sick. My nan worked for 45 years in a textile factory. Paid her taxes every single week, never asked for a thing. She gets £106 a week from the government. That's her reward for a lifetime of service to this country.

Now look at what illegal immigrants and refugees get handed the moment they step off a dinghy:

British pensioner weekly allowance: £106
Illegal immigrant weekly allowance: £250

British pensioner spouse allowance: £25
Illegal immigrant spouse allowance: £225

British pensioner hardship allowance: £0
Illegal immigrant hardship allowance: £100

Total yearly benefit for a British pensioner: £6,000
Total yearly benefit for an illegal immigrant: £29,900

Read those numbers again. Nearly FIVE TIMES more for someone who has never contributed a penny to this country versus someone who spent their entire life building it.

My nan can barely afford to heat her house this winter. She eats one proper meal a day so she can keep the lights on. Meanwhile we're rolling out the red carpet for people who've paid nothing into the system and giving them almost £30k a year of taxpayer money. YOUR money.

And before anyone comes at me with "that's racist" — it's not about race. It's about fairness. It's about priorities. When you treat your own citizens worse than people who arrived yesterday, something is fundamentally broken.

The media won't report on this. The politicians don't want you to see these numbers. They'd rather you stayed distracted arguing about nonsense while they sell this country out from under us. Share this everywhere because they're actively trying to suppress it.

Our pensioners deserve so much better than this. They fought for this country, they built this country, and this is how we repay them. Absolutely disgraceful.

title: Truck full of lab monkeys carrying COVID, herpes & hepatitis C crashes in Mississippi — most escape and authorities are scrambling to cover it up
content:
This story is absolutely insane and the fact that it's barely getting mainstream coverage should tell you everything.

October 28, 2025. A truck hauling rhesus monkeys from Tulane University — one of the biggest biomedical research institutions in the country — crashes on I-59 in Jasper County, Mississippi. Monkeys escape. The Jasper County Sheriff's Department immediately warns the public that these animals are aggressive and carry hepatitis C, herpes, AND COVID-19. Three separate deadly pathogens. In monkeys. Loose on a highway in rural Mississippi.

And what happens next? Tulane swoops in within HOURS and releases a carefully worded statement saying the primates 'aren't infectious.' Just like that. No independent verification. No CDC involvement announced. No public health quarantine zone. Just 'trust us, they're fine.' Does that sound like transparency to you?

Think about this: the sheriff's department said the DRIVER himself told law enforcement the monkeys were dangerous and posed a direct threat to humans. This is the guy literally transporting them. He would know what he's hauling. But suddenly Tulane says nah, nothing to worry about, and everyone's supposed to move on?

The department initially said they 'destroyed' all but one of the escapees, then had to walk that back to THREE still missing once Tulane people showed up. So nobody even knew how many monkeys were on the truck? What kind of operation is this? What else are they transporting on public highways that we don't know about?

Rhesus monkeys are literally the number one primate used in infectious disease research. They are used specifically BECAUSE they can carry human-transmissible diseases. Tulane has entire programs studying exactly these pathogens in these exact animals. But this particular batch? Oh they're totally clean. Sure.

I'm not saying panic. I'm saying ask questions. Why are research primates being moved on public interstates? Why did the official story change three times in 24 hours? And why is nobody in the media pushing back on Tulane's blanket denial?

Something doesn't add up.
